Dear Mr. Holden,

I write to request verifiable assurances that the United States Heartland China Association (hereinafter “Heartland China”) is not operating as an unregistered agent of the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) or the People’s Republic of China (PRC) government and enabling a foreign adversary to covertly influence our local state officials in support of its political objectives.

In November 2023, the Select Committee released its United Front 101 memo, which explains that United Front work is “a unique blend of engagement, influence activities, and intelligence operations”1 used by the CCP to “shape its political environment, including to influence other countries’ policy toward the PRC and to gain access to advanced foreign technology.”2 As part of this whole-of-society strategy, the Chinese government and CCP United Front organizations are utilizing coopted domestic and foreign organizations and elites, which include cultural, civic, and business associations and leaders, as conduits to engage in overt and covert political activities that further its United Front strategy.3

According to Heartland China’s website, the organization is “promoting opportunities between the peoples of the Heartland Region and the People’s Republic of China.”4 While the organization claims that it “does no lobbying,”5 a review of Heartland China’s public activities and partners that are affiliated with the CCP’s influence and intelligence bureaucracy raise serious questions about the validity of this assertion.

Heartland China has a long history of dealings with other associations in the United States whose leaders have extensive ties with the CCP’s United Front system targeting Americans. For example, in 2021 Heartland China cooperated with the United Chinese Americans (UCA), a U.S.-based 501(c)(3) organization to organize a public seminar that criticized the Department of Justice’s counterintelligence efforts against the CCP.6 Public reporting highlights how UCA personnel maintain extensive ties to the CCP’s United Front system7 and are also engaging in political activities in various states.8

Heartland China’s network of domestic and overseas partners further underscores the risk that the organization may be operating in service of foreign malign influence. Congress defined foreign malign influence in law as “…any hostile effort undertaken by, at the direction of, or on behalf of or with the substantial support of, the government of a covered foreign country with the objective of influencing, through overt or covert means… the political, military, economic, or other policies or activities of the United States Government or State or local governments, including any election within the United States; or…the public opinion within the United States.” 9 Heartland China’s Chinese partners include multiple entities that have been identified by the U.S. government as elements of the CCP’s influence and intelligence bureaucracy.

Specifically, Heartland China has repeatedly partnered with the U.S. Chinese People’s Association for Friendship with Foreign Countries (CPAFFC) through programs that bring U.S. local officials to China with the clear aim of influencing their views. These partnerships and relationships raise concerns about the significant entanglement of a foreign adversary with Heartland China’s advocacy. These extensive ties to PRC governmentlinked organizations also raise serious doubts that Heartland China’s many programs – including agricultural roundtables, business seminars, student forums and trips to China hosting U.S. elected officials – may be controlled, directed, and funded by the CCP or PRC governmentlinked entities, and therefore may violate U.S. laws that are intended to ensure transparency in foreign influence and other political activities.

The Foreign Agents Registration Act requires an “agent of a foreign principal”20 engaging in covered “political activities” in the United States to register with the Department of Justice. Covered activities are construed broadly and may include “any activity that the person engaging in believes will, or that the person intends to, in any way influence any agency or official of the Government of the United States or any section of the public within the United States with reference to formulating, adopting, or changing the domestic or foreign policies of the United States or with reference to the political or public interests, policies, or relations of a government of a foreign country or a foreign political party.”21
To better understand Heartland China’s ability to comply with applicable U.S. laws, I request the following documents by 7 May 2026:

1. A list of all programs, including roundtables, seminars, student forums, exchanges, held between Heartland China in China or with Chinese organizations, including a list of participating individuals and entities from January 1, 2021 to December 31, 2025. 2. Records of all contacts—any oral or written communication (including electronic)— made by Heartland China with local U.S. officials, a covered executive branch official or a covered legislative branch official.22 3. Copies of all agreements, amendments, and supplemental records between Heartland China and all of its Chinese partners, including CPAFFC, CAAIE, CCIEE, and CUSEF from January 1, 2021 to December 31, 2025.
4. Records sufficient to show all foreign funding received by Heartland China from the People’s Republic of China and PRC-based entities to the present from January 1, 2021 to December 31, 2025.

The CCP’s United Front operations are persistent, pervasive, and target every level of decision maker in the United States. State and local leaders are especially vulnerable. Heartland China should immediately terminate its relationship with all CCP United Front actors and cease serving as a pawn in the subnational influence operations of our foremost foreign adversary.
